objective: Make Naya Power executable, fail-closed at consequential execution boundaries, and continuously self-tested at the live ChatGPT action boundary.
why: The live host bridge was proven, but consequential execution still needed an explicit claim/state boundary and caller-independent risk derivation before side effects.
changes: Added execution_controller.py with READY → CLAIMED → EXECUTING → OBSERVED → VERIFIED → HANDED_OFF transitions.
Added risk_engine.py with conservative derived risk classification.
Added model_tool_gateway.py requiring claimed execution context and matching derived risk.
Added test_model_tool_gateway.py covering missing claim, valid authorization, and caller-supplied lower-risk rejection.
Extended runtime_activation_check.py to require and self-test the execution boundary.
Extended runtime continuity workflow to compile, validate, and runner-test the new execution boundary.
Updated the live-host runbook to document the claim/gateway boundary.

observations.failure: Sparse checkout attempted to materialize an unrelated legacy repository filename beyond the runner filesystem limit.

observations.result: Kernel 5/5; Orchestrator 3/3; ChatGPT host adapter 4/4; Live host bridge 3/3; Activation gate passed.

Checkout, Python 3.12, compileall, JSON validation, kernel, orchestrator, host adapter, live host, execution controller, risk engine, model/tool gateway, activation gate, and cleanup all completed successfully.

learning: Do not trust model-declared risk; derive risk from action metadata and fail closed on mismatch.
A consequential action needs an explicit execution claim before the tool side effect is authorized.
Execution must have an explicit observation and evidence path before VERIFIED or HANDED_OFF.
Sparse checkout must use a non-cone runtime-only pattern in this repository because of the unrelated legacy long filename.
Integration tests are valuable because they found a real continuation field mismatch that lower-level tests did not expose.
Naya Power does not claim magical interception of hidden model inference; ChatGPT remains the reasoning host and the runtime governs the executable action boundary.
next_action: Use the actual NayaNET Intelligent Hub source as the first real acceptance workload; inspect source of truth, generate candidate actions, pass the selected consequential action through claim/gateway, execute with the authorized host tool, independently verify the exact outcome, record a receipt, promote the learning, and continue to the next highest-value action.
